designSummary: Accuracy estimates against a timestamp reference standard, with calibration and discrimination analyses and subgroup estimates by time of day, weekday and admitting service.
sampleSize: About 38,000 admission decisions over two years, with more than half expected to board four hours or more given a median of 5.1 hours, give confidence intervals of about one percentage point for overall sensitivity and specificity. The binding constraint is the smallest subgroup: night-time surgical decisions, perhaps 2,000, still give intervals of about four percentage points. Because boarding clusters by day through occupancy, intervals use day-level cluster-robust standard errors, which widen them by an amount estimated from the data. More than 100 events in every subgroup meets the usual minimum for calibration assessment.
primaryAnalysis: Sensitivity and specificity of the flag at the deployed threshold with 95 percent confidence intervals using day-level cluster-robust standard errors; the pair is reported together with the number of true and false positives per 1,000 admission decisions.
secondaryAnalysis: Calibration intercept, slope and plot; c statistic of the score and of an occupancy and time-of-day model with the difference and its interval; accuracy by time of day, weekday and admitting service; sensitivity analysis excluding escalated patients.
missingData: Decisions with missing departure times use the pre-specified ward-arrival rule; decisions with neither time are excluded and counted, and a sensitivity analysis treats them first as boarded and then as not boarded.
multiplicity: One primary pair; subgroup estimates are reported with intervals and an interaction test, not as separate claims.
software: R with the pROC and sandwich packages.
overfittingGuards: Reference standard rule fixed before analysis
Threshold taken as deployed, not re-optimised
Subgroups limited to three pre-specified variables
No retraining or recalibration reported as the main result
summary: About 38,000 decisions give narrow intervals; the smallest subgroup and day-level clustering set the precision.
